review_type: Independent source review; reviewer did not implement the change

findings.title: Preserve the new active window when a settings preview loses ownership
findings.scenario: Launch CUBE /C, start Preview, then switch to another window/task or otherwise lose focus/capture while the preview is active.
findings.defect: WM_KILLFOCUS/WM_ACTIVATE/WM_ACTIVATEAPP and the ownership checks clear returnFocus before stop(). However, WM_DESTROY unconditionally calls ShowWindow(config, SW_SHOW) and SetActiveWindow(config) whenever showConfig is true. This activates the already-visible settings dialog independently of the guarded back value in stop().
findings.consequence: The preview dismissal takes active-window/input ownership back from the window the user or Windows just selected. It can interfere with task switching and with the focus/capture handoff that caused teardown.
findings.recommendation: Remove activation from the WM_DESTROY settings branch. The dialog is already visible; let stop() restore previousActive/previousFocus only when its pre-destroy back guard permits it. If visibility later becomes necessary, use a nonactivating show and retain the guarded restoration policy.
evidence: CUBE.C:227 computes back=returnFocus && GetActiveWindow()==w; lines 235-238 restore focus only under back.
CUBE.C:318-324 clear returnFocus on focus/task activation loss; line 332 bypasses it.
The Windows 3.0 SDK documents SW_SHOW as activating, and SetActiveWindow as able to take active-window/input focus.
Native QA sets showConfig=0 at CUBE.C:510, so its existing deactivation case does not exercise this settings-preview branch.

references.title: Microsoft Windows 3.0 SDK Programmer's Reference, Volume 1 (SetActiveWindow and ShowWindow)
